html:
1. Understanding Delaware’s Child Care Market

Child care centers in Delaware operate under the Delaware Office of Child Care Licensing (OCCL), a division of the Delaware Department of Education. The market is foundational to supporting working families and contributing to early childhood development.

Key Market Indicators:

  • Approximately 960 licensed child care programs statewide
  • Waitlists commonly extend to 6 months in high-demand areas like Wilmington
  • Delaware has allocated approximately $11 million annually for early childhood assistance programs (ECAP) through FY 2025
  • Available slots do not meet demand, particularly in New Castle and Sussex Counties

Regional Demand:

  • New Castle County: Highest demand, urban population centers
  • Sussex County: Growing demand with fewer providers
  • Kent County: Moderate demand with some rural access gaps

2. Licensing Requirements

All child care centers must comply with DELACARE regulations (effective July 2024) and obtain licensing under the Delaware Child Care Act (Title 14, Chapter 30A).

Application Process:

  • Submit OCCL licensing application
  • Complete compliance review and facility inspection
  • Background checks for all staff (FBI and state)
  • Health and safety training documentation
  • Fire marshal inspection and approval
  • Zoning compliance verification

Facility Standards:

  • Minimum square footage per child (indoor and outdoor)
  • Age-appropriate equipment and materials
  • Safety barriers, fencing, and playground standards
  • Kitchen and food preparation compliance
  • Adequate restroom facilities by age group

3. Business Structure and Registration

Required Steps:

  • Register business entity with Delaware Division of Corporations
  • Obtain Delaware business license
  • Apply for Employer Identification Number (EIN)
  • Register for state tax accounts
  • Secure appropriate insurance coverage

Insurance Requirements:

  • General liability insurance
  • Professional liability coverage
  • Workers’ compensation
  • Property insurance
  • Vehicle insurance (if providing transportation)

4. Financial Planning

Reimbursement Rates (2024 – Purchase of Care Program):

  • Infant care (full-time): approximately $75.00/day
  • Toddler care: approximately $68.76/day
  • Preschool age: approximately $60.40/day
  • School-age care: lower rates apply
  • Special needs care: eligible for higher supplemental rates

Financial Projections:

  • Providers at 75-85% capacity may achieve 15-25% gross margins
  • Break-even period: 12-18 months
  • Staffing represents 60-70% of operating expenses

Startup Costs:

  • Facility lease/renovation: $50,000 – $200,000
  • Licensing fees: $1,000 – $5,000
  • Equipment and supplies: $20,000 – $75,000
  • Initial staffing: $30,000 – $100,000
  • Working capital: $50,000 – $150,000

5. Staffing Requirements

Delaware mandates specific staff-to-child ratios based on age groups.

Key Positions:

  • Center Director (qualified per DELACARE)
  • Lead Teachers (early childhood education credentials)
  • Assistant Teachers
  • Aides
  • Cook/Food Service Staff

Training Requirements:

  • CPR and First Aid certification
  • Child abuse recognition training
  • DELACARE-specific regulatory training
  • Ongoing professional development hours annually

6. Quality Rating and Improvement

The Delaware Stars Quality Rating & Improvement System (QRIS) provides a framework for continuous quality improvement.

Benefits of Participation:

  • Higher reimbursement rates for subsidized care
  • Marketing advantage with quality designation
  • Access to professional development resources
  • Technical assistance and coaching
  • Parent preference for rated programs

7. Optimal Market Opportunities

  • Infant and toddler care — Higher reimbursement rates and greatest scarcity
  • Special needs programs — Supplemental funding and underserved demand
  • Extended hours/odd-hour care — Serving families with non-traditional schedules
  • Quality-rated programs — Favored by state subsidy programs and families

8. Regulatory Contacts

  • Office of Child Care Licensing (OCCL): Primary licensing authority under Department of Education
  • Delaware Stars QRIS: Quality rating and improvement
  • Purchase of Care Program: State subsidy administration
  • Delaware Department of Education: Oversight authority
